meta.title: Who really said "For attractive lips, speak words of kindness. For lovely eyes, seek out the good in people. For a slim figure, share your food with the hungry"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Not Audrey Hepburn. These “time-tested beauty tips” were written by humorist Sam Levenson in his 1973 book. Hepburn just loved reciting them.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'For attractive lips, speak words of kindness. For lovely eyes, seek out the good in people. For a slim figure, share your food with the hungry'?
meta.ogDescription: Not Audrey Hepburn. Humorist Sam Levenson wrote these lines in his 1973 book In One Era and Out the Other. Hepburn adored and recited them, crediting him.

answer.label: Not Audrey Hepburn — actually Sam Levenson
answer.sourceLine: Written by humorist Sam Levenson in his 1973 book In One Era and Out the Other. Audrey Hepburn cherished the piece and read it aloud to family — and her son recited it at her 1993 funeral — but she always credited Levenson, never claiming it as her own.

source.excerpt: For attractive lips, speak words of kindness. For lovely eyes, seek out the good in people. For a slim figure, share your food with the hungry.
trail: Quote Investigator ↗ traces the lines to Sam Levenson’s 1973 book In One Era and Out the Other, assembled from two separate passages.
Goodreads ↗ attributes the quote to Sam Levenson and tags it “misattributed-audrey-hepburn.”
Per Quote Investigator, Hepburn read the piece to her family and her son recited it at her 1993 funeral — but she credited Levenson, never claiming authorship.
source.excerptNote: The familiar “beauty tips” that circulate online are an assembly of two passages from Levenson’s book — hints he addressed to his daughter and a letter to his newborn granddaughter.

author.name: Sam Levenson
author.heading: About Sam Levenson
author.bio: Sam Levenson was a New York schoolteacher turned humorist, author, and television personality known for warm, folksy reflections on family life. His 1973 book In One Era and Out the Other gathered his gentle wisdom, including the “beauty tips” addressed to his family. He died in 1980, more than a decade before the lines became attached to Audrey Hepburn’s name.

misattribution.heading: Why everyone credits Audrey Hepburn
misattribution.intro: This is one of the internet’s classic “magnet” misattributions: a warm, quotable passage pinned to a beloved star who merely loved reading it aloud.

items.why: Endlessly shared on social media over her image, but Hepburn did not write it. Per Quote Investigator ↗, she recited it to family and credited its real author.

misattribution.truthLine: The lines are Sam Levenson’s, from his 1973 book In One Era and Out the Other; Hepburn simply loved and recited them — per Quote Investigator ↗.

context.heading: How the mix-up spread
lead: Audrey Hepburn genuinely treasured Levenson’s words — she reportedly read them to her sons, and her son Sean recited them at her 1993 memorial. Because the passage travelled so closely with her name and image, the internet gradually dropped Levenson’s name and made Hepburn the “author.”
context.pull: She loved reciting it — and always credited the man who wrote it.
